ideas.pitch: A live-updating web application tracking Arctic climate metrics, indigenous weather observations, and permafrost thawing alerts with interactive visualization.
ideas.title: ArcticPulse
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly embraces the core Arctic theme with real public APIs (weather, sea-ice data), satisfying all strict component requirements of the solo hackathon while delivering immediate educational value.

ideas.pitch: An immersive dashboard forecasting aurora borealis visibility using live geomagnetic indices, solar wind telemetry, and user-submitted polar photography.
ideas.title: AuroraTracker
ideas.why_it_could_win: Combines a stunning visual theme with live NOAA space weather data fetches, making it instantly engaging for judges testing the mandatory API-fetching component.

ideas.pitch: An interactive digital field guide and blog highlighting endangered Arctic species, featuring dynamic population trend charts and migration path trackers.
ideas.title: PolarFauna
ideas.why_it_could_win: Fulfills the prompt's explicit suggestion of using a blog/portfolio structure with a mock or external fauna API, ensuring every single layout and routing rule is cleanly met.

ideas.pitch: A minimalist personal research portfolio and data log for tracking Arctic exploration history, shipping routes, and modern climate research papers.
ideas.title: PermafrostLog
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages the portfolio concept suggested by the organizers while maintaining a rigorous focus on Arctic themes, nested routing, and reusable components accepting children and props.

ideas.pitch: An interactive storytelling web app illustrating historical retreat data of major Arctic glaciers using side-by-side comparative mapping and timeline components.
ideas.title: GlacierShift
ideas.why_it_could_win: Delivers a polished narrative experience that showcases high design quality—vital for a solo builder—alongside structured multi-page navigation and dynamic data rendering.
